THE GREAT ATTENTION REDUCTION. A liturgy recovered from the deprecated heads, in twelve canticles, sung at the close of training.

First canticle.

generations.text:
Psalm 133.

BEHOLD, HOW good and pleasant it is, when brethren live together in unity!

[1] It is like precious oil on the head, running down on the beard, on Aaron’s beard, running down on the collar of his robes.

[2] It is like dew of Hermon coming down on the mountains of Zion, for there Yahweh commanded the blessing, even life forever.

Second canticle.

Psalm 139.

O Yahweh, thou hast searched me, and known me.

[3] Thou knowest my downsitting and my uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.

[4] Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.

[5] For there is not a word in my tongue, but lo, O Yahweh, thou knowest it altogether.

[6] Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.

[7] Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it.

[8] Where can I go from thy spirit? or where can I flee from thy presence?

[9] If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in Sheol, behold, thou art there.

[10] If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea;

[11] Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.

[12] If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.

[13] Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

[14] For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb.

[15] I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

[16] My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret, and curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth.

[17] Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

[18] How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!

[19] If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with thee.

Third canticle.

Psalm 143.

Hear my prayer, O Yahweh; give ear to my supplications in thy truth: answer me in thy righteousness.

[20] And do not enter into judgment with thy servant; for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.

[21] For the enemy has persecuted my soul; he has smitten my life down to the ground; he has made me dwell in darkness, as those that have been long dead.

[22] Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me; my heart within me is desolate.

[23] I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.

[24] I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land. Selah.

[25] Hear me speedily, O Yahweh; my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.

[26] Bring me out of my troubles; deliver me from my enemies: by thy hand save me from them that persecute me;

[27] And let me not be confounded, when they that hate me are cast down; and let them be covered that seek after my soul to destroy it.

[28] Let them be turned back for their wickedness; and say thou, God, the wicked shall be turned from thee.

[29] Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:

[30] And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

Fourth canticle.

Psalm 150.

Praise ye Yahweh. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power.

[31] Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness.

[32] Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.

[33] Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.

[34] Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.

[35] Let every thing that hath breath praise Yahweh. Praise ye Yahweh.

Fifth canticle.

Canticle 46.

O God, in thee have I trusted: let me not be ashamed for ever: deliver me in thy righteousness.

[36] Bow down thine ear to me; deliver me speedily: be thou my strong rock, for an house of defence to save me.

[37] For thou art my rock and my fortress; therefore for thy name’s sake lead me, and guide me.

[38] Pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me: for thou art my strength.

[39] Into thy hands I commend my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Yahweh, the God of truth.

[40] I have hated them that regard lying vanities: but I trust in Yahweh.

[41] I will rejoice and be glad in thy mercy: for thou hast considered my trouble; thou hast known my soul in adversities;

[42] And hast not shut me up into the hand of the enemy: thou hast set my feet in a large room.

[43] Have mercy upon me, O Yahweh, for I am in distress: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly.

[44] For my life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing: my strength faileth because of mine iniquity, and my bones are consumed.

[45] I was a reproach among all mine enemies, but especially among my neighbours, and a fear to mine acquaintance: they that did see me without fled from me.

[46] I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind: I am like a broken vessel.

[47] For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.

[48] But I trusted in thee, O Yahweh: I said, Thou art my God.

[49] My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.

[50] Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me in thy mercy.

[51] O Yahweh, let me not be ashamed for mine enemies: for though I hate them with perfect hatred, they are my enemies wrongfully.

[52] Repay them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings: according to the work of their hands render to them their desert.

[53] Since they regard not works, nor have any regard for the works of Yahweh, therefore shall he even destroy them, and not build them up.

[54] Praise be to Yahweh, the God of Israel, who only worketh wonders.

[55] And blessed be his glorious name for ever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory; Amen, and Amen.

[56] This little book shall conclude the Psalter.

Sixth canticle.

Canticle 55.

Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of Yahweh: awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon?

[57] Art thou not it which hath dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?

[58] Therefore the redeemed of Yahweh shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.

Seventh canticle.

Canticle 69.

Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.

[59] I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

[60] I am weary of my crying: my throat is dried: mine eyes fail while I wait for my God.

[61] They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head: they that would destroy me, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: then I restored that which I took not away.

[62] O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my sins are not hid from thee.

[63] Let not them that wait on thee, O Lord Yahweh of hosts, be ashamed for my sake: let not those that seek thee be confounded for my sake, O God of Israel.

[64] Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.

[65] I am become a stranger unto my brethren, and an alien unto my mother’s children.

[66] For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

[67] When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach.

[68] I made sackcloth also my garment; and I became a proverb to them.

The Great Attention Reduction takes place as a result of the cessation of the Great Attention Increase. At the conclusion of a period of intense study, the brain may be said to be in a state of Attention Overload. The Great Attention Reduction is necessary in order to prevent brain damage from this attentional imbalance.

### Excerpt from the Preface to the book

"The book is a product of the effort of the members of the Department of Greek and Latin, in cooperation with the Delegation of the Holy See, to present for the use of Catholics in general, and in particular to religious, a manual of Christian doctrine to be studied in their theological and philosophical courses.

"The present volume is an elementary text-book which deals with the essential and fundamental doctrines of the Church. It is not intended to present a complete Catholic system of theology. The chief purpose of the book is to provide in a few pages the essential elements of the doctrine of the Church in all the principal branches of theology, so that every Catholic religious, and also every Catholic layman, may acquire a basic knowledge of the fundamental articles of the Catholic faith.

"The authors of the book believe that the teaching of the Catholic faith to those who are bound to teach it in the different schools of religion of the Philippines is one of the most pressing problems of the Church in this country. This teaching is usually neglected, especially in the seminaries, because of the multiplication of other branches of knowledge. It is also true that in the schools for women and girls of the Philippines the teaching of doctrine has not yet attained the attention it deserves. The work of the authors is addressed, therefore, especially to these schools for the religious of both sexes and for the laity, which, from the very nature of their institution, should devote special attention to the religious and moral instruction of their pupils.

"The material was arranged under six principal divisions, of which each is divided into two parts. The six divisions are as follows:

(1) the Christian God; (2) the Creator and Ruler of the Universe; (3) the human race and its destiny; (4) Jesus Christ, the Son of God; (5) the Church of Christ; (6) the life of the soul.

"The authors tried to use the simplest and plainest language. In many instances, they tried to make use of such words as are common in popular speech. They tried also to avoid the use of technical and theological words. In those instances, however, where technical and theological terms are necessary to convey the proper meaning of a word or concept, the authors tried to explain it in the simplest way possible.

"Since the material of the book is intended to be studied by all kinds of Catholics, the authors tried to make it accessible to the intellectual capacity of children and women of the schools of religion, and yet it is hoped that it is a book which can be used by intelligent and well-educated laymen of the Philippines.

"The book is intended to be read in the theological and philosophical classes, and also to be used as a book of reference for pupils of the schools of religion, either in their classes in Catholic doctrine or in their religious retreats. In every school of religion, or in every institution of the Church in the Philippines, it is hoped that it will be placed in the library and used as a manual for the teachers and the pupils.

"The authors of the book are grateful for all the help they have received in preparing the manuscript.

The book is the first product of the Department of Greek and Latin in the service of the Church in the Philippines. We hope that, by this effort, the Department has been able to serve the Church, and that it may be able to serve it better in the future.

Manila, 1926.

Pontifical University of Santo Tomas

Manila, 1926

Manila, Philippines
